heading: Phases protected by matrix product operator symmetries, after Garre-Rubio, Lootens and Molnár
lede: A matrix product operator symmetry generalizes an on-site group action: the symmetry operators are matrix product operators that need not factorize over sites and need not be invertible, and their products are fixed by fusion rules. In 2022 Garre-Rubio, Lootens and Molnár showed that a matrix product state invariant under such an algebra carries fusion and action tensors, that these define F- and L-symbols satisfying a coupled pentagon equation, and that the gauge classes of the L-symbols classify the gapped phases with the symmetry. In Lean the fusion and action tensors, the F- and L-symbols with multiplicity, the coupled pentagon, their gauge freedom, the single-block obstruction, the group case with its anomaly and two-cocycle, and most of the printed examples are proved. The time-reversal constraint, the explicit Fibonacci L-symbol, the coset construction for groups and the phase classification itself remain open.
description: Progress of the Lean 4 formalization of matrix product states symmetric under matrix product operator algebras, arXiv:2203.12563.

routes.heading: Fusion and action tensors, F- and L-symbols
routes.intro: A family of matrix product operators forms an algebra when its operators with arbitrary boundary conditions are closed under multiplication: for every pair of boundaries there is an output boundary, the same at every chain length, whose operator is the product. On periodic chains this gives fusion rules: the product of two operator blocks is a non-negative integer combination of blocks. The matrix product states invariant under such an algebra are described by local data: fusion tensors that reduce a product of two operators to the operators in its decomposition, and action tensors that reduce an operator applied to a state to the states in its decomposition. Comparing two ways of reducing a triple product gives the F-symbols; comparing two ways of reducing two operators applied to a state gives the L-symbols. The two satisfy a coupled pentagon equation, and both are fixed only up to a change of basis of the fusion and action tensors.

stages.title: Arbitrary-boundary closedness and the fusion and action tensors
stages.physics: Closedness with arbitrary boundary conditions, rather than only periodic ones, makes the product of two injective operator blocks an exact sum of blocks: every letter of the product tensor is reconstructed from the blocks, with no remainder. The fusion tensors are the maps into these blocks and their left inverses, and the action tensors arise in the same way. The Perron–Frobenius eigenvector of the fusion matrices gives the quantum dimensions of the labels.
stages.delivers: Fusion and action tensors with multiplicity, their uniqueness up to gauge, and the Perron–Frobenius fusion dimensions.

stages.title: L-symbols with multiplicity and the coupled pentagon
stages.physics: Reducing an operator pair acting on a state in two orders defines the L-symbols, matrices indexed by multiplicity labels. The pentagon equation of the F-symbols has a coupled analogue mixing F and L, and simultaneous changes of basis act on both by an explicit gauge law.
stages.delivers: The L-symbols with multiplicity, the corrected coupled pentagon, and the joint gauge law.

stages.title: No injective state without multiplicity is invariant under an anomalous algebra
stages.physics: If a symmetric state has a single injective block and every action multiplicity is one, the action tensors turn the L-symbols into a trivialization of the F-symbols, so an algebra whose F-symbols are not gauge-trivial has no such state. A single block with higher multiplicity is not excluded: the paper's one-block solution for Rep(S3) has multiplicity two. A positive common eigenvector of the integer action matrices gives a symmetric boundary state.
stages.delivers: The cohomological single-block obstruction and the symmetric boundary state.

routes.heading: Algebras built from a group
routes.intro: When the labels form a group G and the fusion is group multiplication, the F-symbols reduce to a three-cocycle ω and the symmetric states are permuted by G. On the stabilizer H of one block, ω is the coboundary of a two-cochain, and the L-symbols of all blocks are reconstructed from this trivialization.

stages.title: Reconstruction from the stabilizer and its trivializing two-cochain
stages.physics: The L-symbols of a group-like algebra are determined by a subgroup H and a two-cochain β on H with coboundary dβ equal to ω restricted to H. Two such cochains differ by a two-cocycle, and they give the same phase exactly when that two-cocycle is a coboundary, so the solutions form a torsor under the second cohomology group of H. For an injective group representation whose identity operator is the identity and whose fusion is exact, closedness forces an on-site representation with trivial anomaly.
stages.delivers: The reconstruction formula for arbitrary three-cocycles and the torsor of its solutions.

stages.title: Time reversal
stages.physics: If the state and every operator commute with an anti-unitary time reversal, complex conjugation maps the fusion and action data to gauge-equivalent data. The anomaly ω is then cohomologous to a real cocycle. The printed relation for the modulus of the L-symbols fails; the corrected relation states that the ratio of the conjugate L-symbol to the L-symbol is a coboundary.
stages.delivers: The real anomaly is proved; the tensor-level derivation of the corrected L-symbol relation is open.

stages.title: Arbitrary-boundary group operators
stages.physics: For a group with a three-cocycle, the paper builds matrix product operators with arbitrary boundary conditions from a coset construction, and shows that one of the two zipper conditions fails. A weak Hopf algebra average realizes the parent projector of the symmetric boundary.
stages.delivers: The operators, their product and adjoint laws, the zippers and the weak Hopf average are proved; the coset states with the printed action tensors remain.

routes.heading: Classification of phases and examples
routes.intro: Two symmetric states lie in the same phase when a gapped path of symmetric Hamiltonians connects their parent Hamiltonians. The paper shows that the gauge class of the L-symbols is invariant along such a path, and conversely builds a path between any two states with the same class by interpolating their tensors through a mixed tensor.

stages.title: Different L-symbols, different phases; equal L-symbols, one phase
stages.physics: Along a differentiable gapped path the action tensors can be chosen continuously, so the L-symbols, which take values in a discrete set of gauge classes, stay constant. Conversely, two states with the same L-symbols are joined by an interpolation through a mixed tensor whose parent Hamiltonian stays gapped and symmetric.
stages.delivers: The mixed tensor, its interpolation, the uniform gap and the convergence of the ground-space projections are proved for injective endpoints; the commuting symmetric path Hamiltonian, degenerate endpoints and the classification theorem itself remain.

stages.title: Printed examples
stages.physics: Section 6 solves the coupled pentagon for small fusion categories: groups such as ℤ2×ℤ2 with a controlled-Z realization, Rep(S3), su(2)4, and the Fibonacci category, whose indecomposable module is the regular one with L equal to F. Read literally, the printed uniqueness of the two-block Fibonacci solution fails, since two copies of it form another solution; every finite unital action is a direct sum of regular two-block actions.
stages.delivers: The ℤ2×ℤ2 table, the Rep(S3) and su(2)4 module lists, and the decomposition of every Fibonacci action multiplicity into regular two-block actions are proved; the exact action trees and the explicit Fibonacci L-symbol are the remaining part of the Fibonacci example.

glossary: An operator on a chain written as a contraction of one four-legged tensor per site, two physical and two virtual legs.
The decomposition of a product of two symmetry operators as a non-negative integer combination of the operators of the algebra.
A map on the virtual legs that reduces the product of two operators to one operator of its decomposition.
A map on the virtual legs that reduces an operator applied to a symmetric state to one block of the state.
The change of basis between the two orders of reducing a product of three operators.
The change of basis between the two orders of reducing two operators applied to a state.
A function ω of three group elements satisfying the pentagon identity; for a group-like algebra it is the anomaly of the symmetry.
